storyboard.ears: Your gut is a ghost town compared to a hunter-gatherer's.
The Hadza of Tanzania carry about 730 gut bacteria species. The average American has fewer than half that.
storyboard.eyes: substance: bacteria colonies; cause: Data pours the gut culture from a bucket onto the dish and colonies bloom where it lands
storyboard.evidence: Stanford University / Science (Smits et al. 2017) | Gut bacteria species count, Hadza vs average American | https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/modern-hunter-gatherers-have-thriving-gut-microbiome-compared-with-californians | 2026-11-06

storyboard.ears: The secret is fiber. The Hadza eat 150 grams a day, ten times the average American.
storyboard.evidence: Stanford/Science (Smits et al. 2017); U.S. Department of Agriculture | Daily fiber intake: Hadza vs US guideline vs average American | https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/modern-hunter-gatherers-have-thriving-gut-microbiome-compared-with-californians | 2026-11-06

storyboard.ears: The CDC says a third of US antibiotic prescriptions aren't even necessary, and each one can wipe out gut diversity.
storyboard.evidence: U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) | Share of US outpatient antibiotic prescriptions that were unnecessary (2024) | https://www.cdc.gov/antibiotic-use/media/pdfs/2024-Annual-Report-508.pdf | 2026-11-06

storyboard.ears: Civilization made our food safer and our guts emptier.
